biomass_source: marine megafauna / uncertain-FG field reference: DENSITY-DERIVED (not a direct 1994-1996 measurement) - ACCOBAMS Survey Initiative (ASI), Frontiers in Marine Science (2023/2024) synoptic aerial-survey assessment of Mediterranean cetaceans (accobams.org): South-Western Mediterranean strata (3-5) bottlenose dolphin (Tursiops truncatus) density = 0.023 individuals/km2 (range 0.003-0.063, survey year ~2018-2019). Converted to biomass using average adult body mass 217 kg (midpoint of the 135-300 kg adult range reported by Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Bottlenose dolphin' article) = 0.023 x 0.217 t/km2 = 0.004991 t/km2, x an assumed total study area of 175,599 km2 (the sum(strata_area_by_area$area_km2) figure seen in a prior real run of this script - RE-CHECK against the actual current strata_area_by_area.csv total; if it differs, this Biomass_t should be rescaled proportionally, since this script converts Biomass_t back to a density by dividing by the REAL total area at run time, not by the 175,599 km2 assumed here). Caveats: (1) survey year is ~2018-2019, not 1994-1996 - treated as the closest available proxy, not a real measurement of that period; (2) SW Med strata 3-5 approximate but do not exactly match this pipeline's own GSA 1-11 study area; (3) 217 kg is a general adult body-mass midpoint, not Mediterranean-population-specific. - single-species FG with no survey biomass

marine megafauna / uncertain-FG field reference: DENSITY-DERIVED (not a direct 1994-1996 measurement) - ACCOBAMS Survey Initiative (ASI), Frontiers in Marine Science (2023/2024): South-Western Mediterranean strata (3-5) STRIPED DOLPHIN (Stenella coeruleoalba) density = 1 individual/km2 (range 0.53-1.44, survey year ~2018-2019), used as the proxy for the 'Other dolphins' FG since striped dolphin is the dominant species in that bucket for the Western Mediterranean. Converted to biomass using average adult body mass 155 kg (midpoint of the 150 kg female/160 kg male reported on Wikipedia's 'Striped dolphin' article, itself citing standard cetacean references) = 1 x 0.155 t/km2, x an assumed total study area of 175,599 km2 (SAME caveat as BottlenoseDolphins row above - re-check against the real strata_area_by_area.csv total and rescale if different). Caveats: (1) survey-year mismatch, same as above; (2) 'Other dolphins' may also include common dolphin, Risso's dolphin, or other species this pipeline groups together - using striped dolphin alone likely UNDERSTATES the true FG total if those other species have non-trivial abundance in this domain; (3) SW Med strata 3-5 approximate but do not exactly match GSA 1-11. - mixed/multi-species FG, survey has no catch of it at all

marine megafauna / uncertain-FG field reference: DENSITY-DERIVED, COARSE BASIN-WIDE AVERAGE (not stratum-specific, not a direct 1994-1996 measurement) - ACCOBAMS Survey Initiative (ASI), Frontiers in Marine Science (2023/2024), Table 4: whole-Mediterranean corrected fin whale abundance = 3,282 individuals (CV=0.31, survey year ~2018-2019). Converted to a basin-wide average density by dividing by the total Mediterranean Sea area (~2,510,000 km2, the same Mediterranean-wide area figure used elsewhere in this pipeline for the ICCAT swordfish/albacore uniform-density approximation) = 3282/2510000 = 0.0013076 individuals/km2, x average adult body mass 45 t (a commonly-cited order-of-magnitude average for adult fin whales, NOT independently verified against a specific citation in this pass - re-check against a species account e.g. NOAA Fisheries before trusting this number closely) = 0.05884 t/km2, x an assumed total study area of 175,599 km2 (SAME re-check caveat as the rows above). MAJOR CAVEAT: this is a whole-Mediterranean-basin AVERAGE density, not specific to the Western Mediterranean/GSA 1-11 - fin whales are known to concentrate heavily in the Ligurian Sea/Pelagos Sanctuary (adjacent to GSA 7-9) and in the Alboran Sea, so the true Western-Med density could be meaningfully higher OR lower than this basin-wide average depending on how much of GSA 1-11 overlaps those aggregation areas versus open water the species rarely uses. Treat this row as an order-of-magnitude placeholder pending a real Western-Med-specific stratum estimate from the ASI's own sub-area tables (not accessible in this pass - see pipeline_documentation.qmd's Known Gaps section). - single-species FG with no survey biomass

marine megafauna / uncertain-FG field reference: DENSITY-DERIVED, COARSE BASIN-WIDE AVERAGE (not stratum-specific, not a direct 1994-1996 measurement) - proxy built from THREE species this FG is assumed to represent (deep-diving cephalopod-feeders): ACCOBAMS Survey Initiative (Frontiers in Marine Science, 2023/2024), Table 4, whole-Mediterranean corrected abundance: Risso's dolphin (Grampus griseus) 26,006 ind (CV 0.29), long-finned pilot whale (Globicephala melas) 5,540 ind (CV 0.4), Cuvier's beaked whale (Ziphius cavirostris) 2,929 ind (CV 0.4) - combined 34,475 individuals, survey year ~2018-2019. Average adult body mass per species (Wikipedia species articles, midpoints of reported ranges - NOT independently verified against a primary source): Risso's dolphin 0.4 t (300-500 kg range), long-finned pilot whale 3.5 t (crude unweighted mean of the male 'up to 4,500 kg'/female 'up to 2,500 kg' MAXIMUM figures reported - these are maxima, not averages, so this likely OVERSTATES true average mass), Cuvier's beaked whale 2.45 t (1,800-3,100 kg range). Species-level biomass: Risso's 26006x0.4=10,402.4 t; pilot whale 5540x3.5=19,390 t; beaked whale 2929x2.45=7,176.05 t; combined = 36,968.45 t across the whole Mediterranean (~2,510,000 km2) = 0.014729 t/km2 basin-wide average density, x an assumed total study area of 175,599 km2 (SAME re-check-and-rescale caveat as every other row in this file). MAJOR CAVEATS: (1) this is a whole-basin average, not Western-Med-specific - unlike the SpermWhale row above, no Western-Med block-level breakdown for these three species was found in the accessible ASI text; (2) the FG-to-species mapping itself (assuming 'Deep sea-cetacean feeders' = Risso's dolphin + pilot whale + beaked whale) was not verified against this pipeline's own species-to-FG reference file - CONFIRM this against FG_WMed_2026.csv before trusting this row; (3) pilot whale mass uses maximum-weight figures as a stand-in for average, likely overstating this row's contribution. - mixed/multi-species FG, survey has no catch of it at all

marine megafauna / uncertain-FG field reference: DENSITY-DERIVED, REAL WESTERN-MED STRATUM-SPECIFIC DATA (not a direct 1994-1996 measurement) - Boisseau, Reid, Ryan, Moscrop, McLanaghan & Panigada (2024), 'Acoustic estimates of sperm whale abundance in the Mediterranean Sea as part of the ACCOBAMS Survey Initiative', Frontiers in Marine Science, doi:10.3389/fmars.2024.1164026, design-based approach (g(0)=0.912 corrected), survey year ~2018-2019. Block-level density (individuals/1000 km2) and abundance across the Western Mediterranean blocks that map onto GSA 1-11: Block 01 Gulf of Cadiz 3.10 (290 ind, CV 0.43), Block 03 West Algeria 7.22 (641 ind, CV 0.44), Block 04 Balearics 2.66 (246 ind, CV 0.82), Block 05 NE Spain 2.22 (121 ind, CV 0.76), Block 07 West Sardinia 5.90 (431 ind, CV 0.50), Block 8a Gulf of Lion shelf 5.02 (173 ind, CV 0.32), Block 8b Gulf of Lion deep 2.85 (134 ind, CV 0.71) - combined Western-basin total 2,036 individuals across ~483,846 km2 of survey blocks (areas back-calculated from abundance/density per block, summing to the paper's own stated combined total, confirming internal consistency), giving an area-weighted average density of 2036/483846 = 0.004208 individuals/km2 - genuinely Western-Med-specific, not a basin-wide average like the FinWhale row above. Converted to biomass using an average adult body mass of 36 t - a crude UNWEIGHTED mean of the male 'up to 57,000 kg' and female '15,000 kg' adult figures reported by BBC Wildlife/Discover Wildlife (discoverwildlife.com/animal-facts/marine-animals/sperm-whale), NOT sex-ratio-weighted against the Mediterranean population's actual demographic mix (Mediterranean sperm whales are known to be male-biased in some deep-canyon foraging areas, which would push the true average mass, and therefore this Biomass_t, higher) = 0.004208 x 36 = 0.15149 t/km2, x an assumed total study area of 175,599 km2 (SAME re-check-and-rescale caveat as every other row in this file - see BottlenoseDolphins row above). This is the best-sourced row in this file so far: real Western-Med stratum density from a peer-reviewed, ASI-specific paper, not a basin-wide proxy. - single-species FG with no survey biomass

marine megafauna / uncertain-FG field reference: REAL, WESTERN-MED-SPECIFIC ABSOLUTE POPULATION COUNT (not density-derived - this is a direct population figure for the region, so no area-back-out assumption is needed, unlike every other row in this file). Monachus-Guardian species factfile (monachus-guardian.org/factfiles/medit15.htm, citing IUCN Monk Seal specialist group data, most recent consolidated figures collated ~2006 but the source itself notes the population has 'remained numerically stable over the last 30 years' despite ongoing threats, so treat this as a reasonable current order-of-magnitude too): Western Mediterranean sub-population (the small remnant colony centered on the Chafarinas Islands / Alboran Sea, i.e. inside GSA 1) = 11-15 individuals, midpoint 13. NOTE this is separate from the much larger Cabo Blanco colony (~150 individuals, Western Sahara/Mauritania, Atlantic - NOT included here, outside the Mediterranean) and the Eastern Mediterranean sub-population (300-350 individuals, Aegean/Ionian Greece - NOT included, outside GSA 1-11). Converted to biomass using average adult body mass 310 kg (midpoint of the 320 kg male / 300 kg female averages reported on Wikipedia's 'Mediterranean monk seal' article) = 13 x 0.31 = 4.03 t total, for the whole West Med domain directly (no density/area conversion applied, since this already IS a real regional population count, not a density figure needing to be scaled by area). CAVEAT: the source itself explicitly warns these regional figures 'should be treated with caution' given historical underestimation and restricted research access in parts of the Mediterranean - and monk seals are now known to be essentially ABSENT from most of the West Med outside this one remnant colony, so 4.03 t is a genuinely tiny, real figure, not an artifact of missing data. - single-species FG with no survey biomass

marine megafauna / uncertain-FG field reference: REAL REGIONAL BREEDING-SEASON COUNT (a direct count, not density-derived - applied without an area back-out, same convention as the Pinnipeds row above), NOT Western-Med-domain-wide and NOT a direct 1994-1996 measurement. UNEP-MAP RAC/SPA document on seabirds of the Gulf of Lions (rac-spa.org/sites/default/files/doc_open_seas/seabirds_gulf_lions.pdf): Yelkouan shearwater (Puffinus yelkouan, the species this FG's own species list identifies alongside Cory's shearwater/Calonectris diomedea, European storm-petrel/Hydrobates pelagicus, and Balearic shearwater/Puffinus mauretanicus - see FG_WMed_2026.csv FG7) - approximately 10,000 individuals recorded using the Gulf of Lions during the breeding season. Converted to biomass using average adult body mass 488.5 g (midpoint of the 480-497 g range reported by oiseaux.net's 'Puffin yelkouan' species page, Poids/weight field) = 10,000 x 0.0004885 t = 4.885 t. MAJOR CAVEATS: (1) this is ONE regional count (Gulf of Lions only, off the French coast, roughly GSA 7) applied as if representative of the entire FG across the whole Western Med domain, which it is not - the other three species in this FG (Cory's shearwater, storm-petrel, Balearic shearwater) are not counted at all here, so this almost certainly UNDERSTATES the true FG total; (2) survey/count timing not stated precisely by the source, treated as a recent-decades proxy, not a real 1994-1996 measurement; (3) 'individuals using the area' during breeding season is not the same as a resident breeding population - some double-counting or transient birds are possible. Retained despite these caveats because it is the only real, citable regional seabird count found for this FG after extensive search (2026-09-24/25) - a genuine floor estimate, not a full census. - mixed/multi-species FG, survey has no catch of it at all

marine megafauna / uncertain-FG field reference: REAL CONTINENT-SCALE POPULATION ESTIMATE, PARTIALLY BACKED OUT TO EXCLUDE A KNOWN NON-MEDITERRANEAN COLONY (a direct population count, not density-derived - applied without an area back-out, same convention as PelagicSeabirds/Pinnipeds above), NOT Western-Med-domain-specific and NOT a direct 1994-1996 measurement. CIESM Mediterranean Science Commission seabird guide (ciesm.org/seabird-guide/audouins-gull/): Audouin's gull (Ichthyaetus/Larus audouinii - one of the species in this FG's own species list, FG8 in FG_WMed_2026.csv, alongside other Larus/Sterna/Phalacrocorax spp.) total population '43,000-44,000 mature individuals in Europe alone', with the CIESM page itself identifying the Ebro Delta (NE Spain) and Chafarinas Islands (off NE Morocco) - both within this pipeline's own GSA 1-11 domain - as the species' 'main colonies', separate from a more recently established, and explicitly non-Mediterranean, Atlantic colony at Ilha Deserta de Faro, Portugal ('approximately 4,200 pairs' = ~8,400 individuals, per the same CIESM page). Subtracting the Portugal Atlantic colony from the Europe-wide total: (43,500 midpoint - 8,400) = ~35,100 individuals treated as the Western-Med-domain proxy count. Converted to biomass using average adult body mass 517.5 g (midpoint of the 500-535 g range reported by oiseaux.net's 'Audouin's Gull' species page, Poids/weight field) = 35,100 x 0.0005175 t = 18.16 t. MAJOR CAVEATS: (1) 'mature individuals in Europe' minus one known Atlantic colony is a crude proxy for 'Western Mediterranean population', not a real regional count - some of the remainder may still be Eastern Mediterranean (Greece/Turkey/Cyprus colonies exist) rather than Western; (2) only Audouin's gull is counted - the other species in this FG (Larus genei, L. melanocephalus, L. michahellis, Chroicocephalus ridibundus, Phalacrocorax aristotelis/carbo, Sternula albifrons, Sterna hirundo, Gelochelidon nilotica, Thalasseus sandvicensis) are not, so this likely UNDERSTATES the true FG total considerably (several of these, e.g. the yellow-legged gull Larus michahellis, are individually far more numerous than Audouin's gull); (3) a global Wikipedia figure for the same species ('population of about 10,000 pairs', undated) is roughly HALF the individual-count implied by the CIESM figure once pairs are doubled - the two sources are not fully reconciled, CIESM's more specific numeric breakdown was preferred here; (4) count timing not stated precisely, treated as a recent-decades proxy, not a real 1994-1996 measurement. - mixed/multi-species FG, survey has no catch of it at all

marine megafauna / uncertain-FG field reference: DENSITY-DERIVED FROM TRACKED INDIVIDUALS WITHIN ONE MPA (not a basin-wide survey, not a direct 1994-1996 measurement) - Abalo-Morla, S., Marco, A., Martins, S., Camino, M., Bellido, J.J., Castillo, J.J., Ferrandis, E., Fraga, A., Munoz-Perez, J.J., & Camino, R. (2022), 'Assessing the use of marine protected areas by loggerhead sea turtles (Caretta caretta) tracked from the western Mediterranean', Global Ecology and Conservation, 38, e02196: satellite-tracked adult/subadult loggerhead turtles yielded an estimated in-MPA density of 0.001 individuals/km2 within the 'Mediterranean Cetacean Corridor' candidate MPA (60,965 km2, a deep-pelagic corridor spanning the Alboran Sea/Western Mediterranean, overlapping GSA 1 and adjacent GSAs). Converted to biomass using average adult body mass 135 kg (Wikipedia 'Loggerhead sea turtle' article, average adult figure) = 0.001 x 0.135 = 0.000135 t/km2, x an assumed total study area of 175,599 km2 (SAME re-check-and-rescale caveat as every other row in this file - see BottlenoseDolphins row above) = 23.71 t. MAJOR CAVEATS: (1) this density comes from a tracked-individual habitat-use study inside ONE candidate MPA, not a population survey - it reflects how intensively that specific corridor is used by tagged turtles, not necessarily the true average density across the whole West Med domain, which could be considerably higher (turtles also use continental-shelf foraging/nesting areas this corridor does not cover) or lower; (2) 135 kg is a general adult average, not Mediterranean-population-specific and not stage-structured (this FG likely also includes juveniles/subadults with much lower individual mass, which would push the true average FG body mass down and this Biomass_t down accordingly); (3) survey/tracking period is ~2010s, not 1994-1996 - treated as the closest available proxy. - single-species FG with no survey biomass

ICCAT stock assessment (SSB): THIS COLUMN HOLDS A DENSITY (t/km2), NOT A TONNAGE - see ICCAT_STOCK_AREA_KM2 in 01_biomass.R (stock_area_km2=1 for BFT, a deliberate pass-through). Real, direct GBYP aerial-survey biomass density from the Balearic Sea 'A-core' spawning-aggregation survey block (CREEM's statistical analysis of ICCAT GBYP Phase 11 aerial survey data: https://iccat.int/GBYP/DOCS/Aerial_Survey_Phase_11_CREEM_2021_Data_Analysis.pdf), average of 2017 (130.54 kg/km2), 2018 (217.84 kg/km2), 2019 (188.38 kg/km2), 2021 (76.27 kg/km2) = 153.26 kg/km2 = 0.1532575 t/km2. Chosen over an area-ratio split of the whole East Atlantic+Mediterranean SSB because that stock spans a far larger, non-uniformly-occupied range (mostly Atlantic, concentrating in the Med only to spawn) - an area ratio there would be invented, not sourced. Caveats: (1) spawning-season snapshot, not an annual average - likely overstates the true year-round mean; (2) A-core-block density applied here as the whole West Med domain average, same simplification already used for Posidonia/gorgonians in claude/benthic_habitat_megafauna_biomass_sourcing_guide.md; (3) 2017-2021 survey data used as a stand-in for 1995 - GBYP itself only began around 2010, no aerial survey existed in 1995. -- TEMPORAL MISMATCH: this density is from a 2017-2021 GBYP aerial survey, applied as-is to the 1994-1996 baseline. ICCAT SCRS 2022 BFT-E assessment (ASAP model, Collect. Vol. Sci. Pap. ICCAT 79(3), SCRS/2022/013): SSB declined from the 1970s to a trough ~2007, then rose steadily 2010-2020 to the highest level since the 1960s - so 1995 SSB was LOWER than 2017-2021. No citable numeric ratio found in the SCRS report tables checked (SSB-by-year is graphical/appendix-only there) - NOT numerically adjusted. Likely OVERESTIMATES 1995 biomass - review before trusting as a baseline value. - single-species FG with no survey biomass

ICCAT stock assessment (SSB): APPROXIMATION - closest available, not measured for 1995 specifically. CORRECTED 2026-09-27: the previous version of this row used 13,325 t, which is MSY (maximum sustainable YIELD - a sustainable catch RATE, t/year) mislabeled as 'B_MSY'. MSY and Bmsy (biomass at MSY - a stock SIZE, t) are different quantities that both appear in the same exec summary; using MSY as if it were biomass understated swordfish biomass by roughly 5x. The correct absolute biomass reference point is Bmsy = 71,319 t (joint posterior median across model variants, 67,509-73,928 t range), from the JABBA surplus-production model in ICCAT's own 2020 Mediterranean swordfish stock assessment (https://www.iccat.int/Documents/Meetings/Docs/2020/REPORTS/2020_SWO_MED_ENG.pdf). Combined with B2018/BMSY = 0.72 (https://www.iccat.int/Documents/SCRS/ExecSum/SWO_MED_ENG.pdf) -> B2018 = 0.72 x 71,319 = 51,350 t (whole Mediterranean stock). No public year-by-year SSB table exists (SCRS reports show this only as a graph, not tabulated), so this single 2018 point is used as the closest available figure to the 1995 Ecopath baseline - same 'closest available, flagged not guessed' convention as every other manual-cited source in this pipeline (see claude/benthic_habitat_megafauna_biomass_sourcing_guide.md). -- TEMPORAL MISMATCH: this density is from a 2018 JABBA model estimate, applied as-is to the 1994-1996 baseline. ICCAT SCRS 2020 SWO-MED assessment (JABBA Bayesian state-space model): stock was already overfished by the mid-1990s (sharp 1950-1970 decline), with only modest further decline 1996-2010 before accelerating decline into 2018 - so 1995 biomass was likely HIGHER than the 2018 estimate used here. No citable numeric ratio found - NOT numerically adjusted. Likely UNDERESTIMATES 1995 biomass, probably by a smaller margin than BFT's overestimate - review before trusting. - single-species FG with no survey biomass

benthic habitat (seagrass/macroalgae/coralligenous): Bernardeau-Esteller et al. 2023, Diversity 15(1):101 (https://www.mdpi.com/1424-2818/15/1/101) - Posidonia oceanica leaf biomass 280 +/- 30 g DW/m2 (437 shoots/m2 x 0.633 g DW/shoot), Cala Sardina (Cadiz), measured at 2-4 m depth in Aug-Sep 2021. DEPTH FACTOR 0.6: the model only counts meadow deeper than 10 m; leaf biomass falls with depth mainly through shoot density, with near-constant shoot weight (Olesen et al. 2002, Mar. Ecol. Prog.
